title: Isolation-based Spherical Ensemble Representations for Tabular Anomaly Detection
Isolation-based Spherical Ensemble Representations for Tabular Anomaly Detection
summary: Unsupervised tabular anomaly detection suffers from conflicting distributional assumptions, quadratic complexity and weak handling of local anomalies; ISER addresses this by sampling psi-point subsets, building hyperspheres whose nearest-neighbour radii act as a monotonic proxy for local density, and encoding every point as a t-dimensional ensemble representation (phi = 1 - 1/r when covered, phi = 1 otherwise). Two scores are derived from that representation - the arithmetic mean (ISER-A) and the cosine similarity to the all-ones anomaly reference (ISER-S) - and the same representation is reused as a transformed feature space for an inverted-path-length Isolation Forest (ISER-IF). Averaged over 5 runs on 20 real-world datasets, ISER-S reaches the best average AUC-ROC of 0.8523 (ISER-A 0.8399) against 12 baselines, and ISER-IF improves iForest on all nine datasets in Table IV, e.g. 0.8530 -> 0.9314 on Ionosphere.

Datasets are the .npz files shipped inside the authors' repository

from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score

def find_npz(name):
    """Locate repo/data/*_<name>.npz (case-insensitive on the name part)."""
    cand = os.path.join(DATA_DIR, name)
    if os.path.exists(cand):

"""Reproduce the ISER-IF AUC-ROC result on real benchmark data (Table IV row),
plus the ISER-S / ISER-A sibling scores and a PyOD iForest baseline, from
scratch using the authors' released code (repo/ISER.py, used verbatim) and
the datasets bundled in that repository (repo/data/*.npz).

Default run (what the verifier executes):
    python reproduce.py
-> sweeps psi in {2,4,...,256} x 5 seeds on Ionosphere, t = 200 partitionings,
   selects psi per method by argmax of the 5-seed mean AUC-ROC, and writes
   results/metrics.json with the ISER-IF headline value.

All numbers in the output JSON are computed from data in this run; no
published values are embedded anywhere in the code.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import time

import numpy as np

from common import load_dataset, iforest_baseline
from iser_eval import run_psi_grid

DEFAULT_PSI_GRID = [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256]  # {2^m, m=1..8}, paper Sec. V-A
DEFAULT_SEEDS = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]                       # 5 repetitions, paper Sec. V-A


def run_dataset(name, psi_grid, seeds, t, run_baseline=True, verbose=True):
    X, y = load_dataset(name)
    n, d = X.shape
    n_anom = int(y.sum())
    if verbose:
        print("=== %s: X%s, anomalies=%d (%.2f%%) ==="
              % (name, X.shape, n_anom, 100.0 * n_anom / n), flush=True)

    block = {
        "n_samples": int(n),
        "n_features": int(d),
        "n_anomalies": n_anom,
        "anomaly_rate": n_anom / n,
    }

    t0 = time.time()
    grid = run_psi_grid(X, y, psi_grid, seeds, t=t, verbose=verbose)
    block["t_partitionings"] = t
    block["psi_grid"] = [int(p) for p in psi_grid]
    block["seeds"] = [int(s) for s in seeds]
    block["methods"] = {m: grid[m] for m in ("ISER_A", "ISER_S", "ISER_IF")}
    block["elapsed_sec_grid"] = grid["elapsed_sec"]

    if run_baseline:
        b = iforest_baseline(X, y, seeds=seeds)
        block["iforest_baseline"] = {
            "mean": float(np.mean(b)),
            "std": float(np.std(b)),
            "per_seed": [float(v) for v in b],
            "config": "PyOD IForest(n_estimators=100, max_samples=256), full data",
        }
        iser_if = block["methods"]["ISER_IF"]["mean"]
        block["iser_if_relative_improvement_over_iforest_pct"] = (
            100.0 * (iser_if - block["iforest_baseline"]["mean"])
            / block["iforest_baseline"]["mean"])
    block["elapsed_sec_total"] = time.time() - t0
    return block


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--datasets", default="Ionosphere",
                    help="comma-separated; first one is the headline metric")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=os.path.join("results", "metrics.json"))
    ap.add_argument("--t", type=int, default=200)
    ap.add_argument("--seeds", default=",".join(str(s) for s in DEFAULT_SEEDS))
    ap.add_argument("--psi-grid", default=",".join(str(p) for p in DEFAULT_PSI_GRID))
    ap.add_argument("--no-baseline", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    names = [s.strip() for s in args.datasets.split(",") if s.strip()]
    seeds = [int(s) for s in args.seeds.split(",") if s.strip()]
    psi_grid = [int(p) for p in args.psi_grid.split(",") if p.strip()]

    t_start = time.time()
    results = {}
    for name in names:
        results[name] = run_dataset(name, psi_grid, seeds, args.t,
                                    run_baseline=not args.no_baseline)

    head = names[0]
    iser_if = results[head]["methods"]["ISER_IF"]
    metrics = {
        "metric": "AUC-ROC",
        "value": iser_if["mean"],
        "dataset": head,
        "split": "full contaminated dataset, no train/test split "
                 "(unsupervised/transductive)",
        "config": {
            "method": "ISER-IF (Isolation Forest on the ISER ensemble "
                      "representation, inverted scoring S = 1 - 2^(-E(h)/c(n)))",
            "code": "authors' repo/ISER.py used verbatim "
                    "(https://github.com/charles-cao/ISER)",
            "t_partitionings": args.t,
